statements.description: The hub restore drill starts an old backup, returns clients to current checkpoints, and restores a nested view.
statements.remarks: Your organization chooses backup schedules and recovery.

statements.description: The hub restore drill exercises recovery from a cold backup without retaining signing or encryption keys in that backup.
statements.remarks: Your organization approves and records recovery exercises.

implemented-requirements.description: On Kubernetes each hub runs hardened.

statements.description: When the site stack deploys hubs on Kubernetes, each hub is a StatefulSet of one replica that runs as user 65532 with a read-only root filesystem, no privilege escalation, every capability dropped, the RuntimeDefault seccomp profile, no service account token and a memory limit; its health check is its liveness and readiness probe, its TLS, signing and encryption key files are mounted from Secrets with mode 0440, its volume is on the encrypted site class, and no autoscaler is rendered.
statements.remarks: Your organization lists the site's hubs in the site file and runs them on the site's cluster.

implemented-requirements.description: Each hub ends its own TLS and is not behind the shared ingress.

statements.description: When the site stack deploys hubs on Kubernetes, several hubs on one site each render as their own StatefulSet with their own volume, and no Ingress in the site stack routes to any hub. Sessions reach a hub at its cluster address and members at its node port, both plain TCP to the hub's own TLS on port 8443, and each hub's server certificate is issued by site-pki-hub for its site name and cluster names.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides which projects each hub serves and which members may reach its node port.

control-implementations.description: Statements about the hub from the 44.1 coverage work (44.1-11).

implemented-requirements.description: The hub admits a device only as the project's signed roster says, and drops it when the roster revokes it.

statements.description: The hub follows each project's signed roster for who may connect. A device the roster does not have gets no session, and once the roster records device.revoke the device's token is refused and a new session is refused too. Only the staff lead's or deputy's device can register an invitation, and an invitation the roster records as used is refused. CI tests of the hub prove each of these, on the same hub code a self-hosted container and a Kubernetes site run.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides who may lead a staff project, approves each person's admission, reviews the roster on its own schedule and removes people who leave.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub logs its events as JSON lines with an event name, redacted before they are written.

statements.description: The hub logs the events it handles (start and refused start, the join desk's outcomes, state directory changes, checkpoint conflicts) as one JSON line each, with time, level and event name first. A refused setting stops the hub with one hub.start_refused line naming the setting, never its value, and join desk lines carry only the project id, the invitation id and a reason word. CI tests of the hub's logger prove each of these.
statements.remarks: Your organization selects the events it needs from each component, collects the hub's log lines, and decides how long it keeps them.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub detects and stops join secret guessing, a device that signs two entries at one place, and floods.

statements.description: The hub watches for misuse and stops it. After five join posts with a wrong MAC an invitation is locked; a device that signs two entries at one place is quarantined and its token refused; and calls past the per-address and per-writer rates are refused with Retry-After. CI tests of the hub prove each of these.
statements.remarks: Your organization collects the hub's log lines, watches them with its other monitoring, and responds to what they show.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub's configuration is a fixed set of HUB_ settings with safe defaults; anything else stops it.

statements.description: The hub's configuration is a fixed set of HUB_ settings. Without them it listens only on 127.0.0.1, port 8443, with the default state directory and no public address. An unknown HUB_ name, a relative state directory, a bad port, host or public address stops it, without the value being repeated. The hub has no runtime package dependencies. CI tests of the hub prove each of these.
statements.remarks: Your organization records the settings it runs each hub with as its baseline and reviews changes to them.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub refuses to start on a Node.js older than 26.13.1 and has no runtime package dependencies.

statements.description: The hub refuses to start on a Node.js release older than 26.13.1, naming the version it needs, and has no runtime package dependencies, so a fix to it arrives as a new hub release or a Node.js update. CI tests of the hub prove the version check and the empty dependency list.
statements.remarks: Your organization installs Node.js and hub updates within the time it sets for security fixes.

implemented-requirements.description: A revoked device loses its token and open stream at once.

statements.description: As soon as the roster records device.revoke, the hub refuses the device's token, refuses a new session, and closes the device's open event stream. CI tests of the hub prove each of these.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides when a person poses a risk and has the staff lead revoke their devices within the time it sets.

implemented-requirements.description: The hub sends each device only the cells it holds.

statements.description: The hub passes a project's entries only to devices that hold the cell they are in: a member sees only the streams and grant hashes of its cells, a member of one compartment receives no frame, page or blob of another, and a device not on a cell's access list cannot post presence to it. CI tests of the hub prove each of these.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides which people are cleared for which compartments.

implemented-requirements.description: Only the lead's or deputy's device registers invitations and reads join requests; a hub device gets no session.

statements.description: On the hub only the staff lead's or deputy's device can register an invitation or list join requests; a member's device is refused 403. The hub's own device, admitted to hold the project, gets no person session. A member cannot write a roster entry such as member.invite. CI tests of the hub prove each of these.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides who holds the lead and deputy roles.

implemented-requirements.description: A member's device cannot run the lead's functions on the hub.

statements.description: A member's device cannot register an invitation, list join requests or write a roster entry reserved for the lead and deputy: the hub refuses each. CI tests of the hub prove each refusal.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides who holds the lead and deputy roles.

implemented-requirements.description: A hub session token ends after 15 minutes.

statements.description: A hub session token works for 15 minutes and is then refused; the device opens a new session with a fresh signed answer. A device holds at most 8 tokens per project. CI tests of the hub prove both.
statements.remarks: Your organization sets how long its people's editor sessions may stay signed in.

implemented-requirements.description: Devices reach the hub only over TLS 1.3.

statements.description: Devices reach the hub only over TLS 1.3: a client limited to TLS 1.2 fails the handshake and a plain HTTP client gets no answer. CI tests of the built hub prove both.
statements.remarks: Your organization decides from which networks its people may reach the hub.
